Finding.Text: "Where a change lives" says of a directory under closed/ without records/close.xml that "its first error names the missing close record", and conformance.md CL-03 says "the first error naming the missing close record". The kernel orders contract defects before the layout defects (src/state.ts: malformed = contractDefects[0] ?? locationDefects[0] ?? records.defects[0]), so the sentence holds only when the contract is readable and matches the directory. Probed: closed/C-0098-empty without contract.xml lists as "malformed: contract.xml is missing" and check prints the close-record defect second; closed/C-0096-mismatch with a foreign contract lists as "malformed: contract.xml: id ... is not the directory name ...". The directory is reported malformed in every case, so the behaviour the contract requires holds; the two sentences overstate which error comes first. A wording fix in the documents, or the layout defect ordered first in the kernel, either way a decision for the author.

CK6 asserts that the status --all output includes the two ids, not that it carries the lines "C-0001-kernel: closed" and "C-0002-pilot-readiness: closed". The listing prints every directory under closed/ with its id, as "id: closed" or as "id: malformed: ...", so the substring test adds nothing to the filesystem test before it and would pass if the kernel located the two moved changes but failed to read their records. A contract that reuses this pattern should match the whole line.
